CEST-detectable metabolite candidates: breast

2 of 9 candidates clear the simulated with-vs-without contrast threshold (0.5%) at some field strength, by chemical exchange (downfield, +ppm) or by the relayed NOE (upfield, −ppm). 1 fall below it; 6 are unknown because no group had a verified reference rate, so nothing could be simulated. The threshold applies to our own simulation, never to a literature MTRasym.

Excluded before simulation (not stored in the tissue): [model's own exclusion] Total creatine (creatine + phosphocreatine) -- rejected as a 1H MRS spectroscopic category label summing two distinct molecules with no single definable unit; no single-molecule creatine or phosphocreatine mM value for breast was retrieved, and breast (non-muscle) tCr is likely sub-mM; [model's own exclusion] Lactose in breast milk (~60 g/L = ~347 mM) -- excluded because breast milk is a ductal/alveolar secretion, not a metabolite stored in breast tissue parenchyma; per rules, secretions are not CEST targets of the tissue itself; [model's own exclusion] Total choline / phosphomonoesters (PME) / phosphodiesters (PDE) -- 31P and 1H MRS peak groupings of chemically unrelated compounds, not single molecules or polymers with definable repeating units; [model's own exclusion] Lipid CH2 / triglycerides / free fatty acids -- chemically heterogeneous, dominant protons are non-exchangeable CH2, not a CEST pool (PMIDs 30830375, 18516631); [model's own exclusion] Glycogen -- no quantitative tissue-stored data found; breast parenchyma is adipose-dominated with no documented significant glycogen store; glycoCEST not a meaningful target in breast; [model's own exclusion] Glutathione (GSH) -- intracellular concentration in mammalian cells is typically mM range, but no breast-specific verbatim mM quote was retrieved in this session; flag for follow-up; has 1 amide NH and 2 -OH so is CEST-relevant; [model's own exclusion] 31P-only species (ATP, Pi, phosphocreatine as 31P peaks) -- rejected per rules unless naming the actual molecule for its 1H exchangeable groups; PCho and PEA are reported as molecules, not as 31P peaks

Mobile protein/peptide amide pool (APT) — CEST: ✓ detectable (rNOE)

Concentration: 250.00 mM typical (~200-300 mM of mobile amide-proton-equivalent (per exchangeable NH, 1 per amide residue); the CEST-exchangeable mobile fraction of the ~1 M tissue protein-backbone amide pool)

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: Estimate of the MOBILE amide-proton-equivalent pool, NOT the intact-protein molarity (a protein is one huge molecule at a tiny molar concentration even though its amide pool is abundant). Total protein in solid mammalian tissue is ~100-150 mg/mL (Bergmeyer tissue tables); with ~110 Da per residue that is ~900-1400 mM of backbone amide NH sites (~1 M amide-proton equivalent). The mobile, CEST-exchangeable NH fraction in soft tissue is reported in the APT literature to be on the order of ~200-300 mM amide-proton equivalent (a significant fraction of the backbone pool being mobile in soft tissue, higher than in highly crosslinked ECM). A central ~250 mM is used here. PMID 31136039 confirms the APT signal in human breast is dominated by mobile protein concentration, validating the pool's relevance; no breast-specific absolute mobile-amide mM was quoted in the abstracts retrieved, so this is an order-of-magnitude estimate anchored to the APT-literature 200-300 mM mobile-pool range.

Recommended field strength(s): 0.5 T, 1.5 T, 3 T, 5 T, 7 T

Robustness to input uncertainty: robust

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (aliphatic C-H (mobile protein, rNOE) [rnoe]: concentration 200-300 mM, kex fixed at 5 s−1 (single measurement, spread unknown)) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 4.39-6.40%, 1.5 T: 7.75-11.20%, 3 T: 9.21-13.25%, 5 T: 9.99-14.36%, 7 T: 10.38-14.89%. Threshold 0.5%. Detectable even at the low corner.

Frequency-collision analysis:

  • The 3.5 ppm amide has no overlap warnings at any field and is cleanly separated from all other candidates.
  • The -3.5 ppm rNOE is the crowded pool: at 0.5 T it blurs with GAG-OH (92 Hz) and myo-inositol (90 Hz), and at ALL fields it blurs with the semisolid MT pool at -2.4 ppm (23 Hz at 0.5 T vs a ~15,937 Hz MT linewidth), so the rNOE is essentially buried under MT at low field and only partially separates as field rises (234 Hz at 5 T, 328 Hz at 7 T).
  • At 0.5 T the rNOE cannot be claimed as a resolved CEST peak.

Direct water saturation: Swept B1 is 0.25 µT at every field, giving a direct-saturation bandwidth of only 10.6 Hz. Both the 3.5 ppm amide (175 Hz at 0.5 T to 2.45 kHz at 7 T) and the -3.5 ppm rNOE sit far outside this footprint, so there is no direct-water masking. This is why the sweep sits at the B1 floor: slow-exchange pools peak at low B1 and any increase only adds direct water saturation.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat:

  • The amide kex=65.5 s−1 is borrowed class-level from human BRAIN (PMIDs 40228056, 23008121), with no breast-specific measurement, pH/T/field unstated, spread 15-158 s−1. The rNOE rate (5 s−1) is borrowed from PROTEIN PHANTOMS/solutions (PMID 25996515), a class-level value with NO stated uncertainty (kex_spread null).
  • The dominant-contrast group therefore rests on a phantom rate; these are frequently not the in-vivo breast rate (pH, T, crowding shift kex, sometimes an order of magnitude). Read contrast as order-of-magnitude, not precise. The APT peak's detectability is independently confirmed in breast, which rescues the amide verdict.

Optimized saturation sequence by field strength (derived from a Bloch-McConnell B1×Tsat sweep):

  • 0.5 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Slow-exchange rNOE peaks at the lowest B1; the 10.6 Hz direct-sat bandwidth leaves the -3.5 ppm pool unmasked. The long 3 s saturation is needed to build up the slow 5 s−1 relay. Amide (2.103%) is also above threshold and uses the same low-B1/long-Tsat prescription.
    recommended sequence: 5.408% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 1.5 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Same slow-exchange logic; Hz separation has grown so the pool is cleaner. Low B1 keeps direct water saturation negligible.
    recommended sequence: 9.511% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 3 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Amide (7.368%) clearly co-detectable at this field; low B1 keeps the direct-sat footprint minimal and favors the slow-exchange amide.
    recommended sequence: 11.274% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 5 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — rNOE begins to separate from MT (234 Hz). Slow exchange still favors the B1 floor.
    recommended sequence: 12.223% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 7 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Amide (8.916%) and rNOE (12.687%) both strong; still prefer low B1 because the amide is slow-exchanging and higher B1 would only add direct water saturation.
    recommended sequence: 12.687% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied

B1/Tsat vs. extraction method (click for note + literature)

Note: For the 3.5 ppm amide, MTRasym is acceptable in breast but fat contamination forces Dixon or a fat-corrected normalization (PMID 31532006, 35476934). For the upfield rNOE at -3.5 ppm, multi-pool Lorentzian fitting, MTRREX, or AREX is strongly preferred over MTRasym because the rNOE overlaps MT and other upfield pools. PMID 41553443 is directly on point: in murine breast APTw-CEST, MTRREX and AREX separated subtypes while MTRasym showed none. Use AREX (low-B1, slow-exchange, removes T1/direct-sat bias) or five-pool Lorentzian fitting.

Caveats / critique (5 points, 257 words) — 250 mM mobile-protein amide is a defensible mid-tissue value for a protein-rich parenchymal/stromal pool, consistent with PMID 31136039 which attributes breast …
  • 250 mM mobile-protein amide is a defensible mid-tissue value for a protein-rich parenchymal/stromal pool, consistent with PMID 31136039 which attributes breast APT largely to mobile protein concentration rather than pH. The 200-300 mM range is sound. Caveat: in a fat-heavy breast the accessible mobile-protein fraction varies, so contrast is tissue-dependent. This number is load-bearing for the simulated contrast.
  • AGREE with all three classes: backbone NH=amide (correct); side-chain Asn/Gln NH=amide co-resonating at 3.5 ppm reinforcing the same peak (correctly handled, no separate group needed); aliphatic C-H=rnoe (correct non-exchangeable mobile pool, upfield). No exchangeable protons neglected. Minor: Agent 2 estimated rNOE at -3.2 ppm but the table median used is -3.5 ppm; acceptable.
  • Amide in vivo is reported at 3.0-3.6 ppm across brain/liver/abdomen (PMIDs 23400954, 26845067, 26334509); the simulated 3.5 ppm is central and matches the in-vivo range. No breast-specific shift documented, so no conflict. None material. Amine termini are a tiny fraction blending into the broad amide region and not a distinct resolvable CEST peak; not worth flagging.
  • no SAR or hardware ceiling is applied: the recommended B1/Tsat is the sweep optimum, and deliverability must be checked against the scanner's SAR monitor Primary 1H CEST target in breast at 3.5 ppm. Report as the mobile amide-PROTON pool concentration (mM of exchangeable NH), NOT intact-protein molarity. n_exchangeable_protons = 1 per amide residue.
  • Dominant endogenous APT contrast in human breast (PMID 31136039, n=22, 7T). [Unsourced reasoning] 1 numeric step(s) rest on an unsourced assumption: 'Mobile, CEST-exchangeable amide NH pool in soft tissue is typically ~2'.

Recommended field strength(s): 7 T

Robustness to input uncertainty: fragile

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (ring/side hydroxyl OH [hydroxyl]: concentration 1-10 mM, kex fixed at 600 s−1 (single measurement, spread unknown)) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 0.01-0.08%, 1.5 T: 0.02-0.18%, 3 T: 0.04-0.41%, 5 T: 0.08-0.80%, 7 T: 0.12-1.15%. Threshold 0.5%. Only the point estimate clears the threshold; the low corner does not.

Frequency-collision analysis:

  • The hydroxyl (0.82 ppm) is the real problem: at EVERY field it blurs with myo-inositol (0.72 ppm; 2.1 Hz at 0.5 T to 29.8 Hz at 7 T, all << the ~223 Hz combined linewidth), so GAG-OH cannot be separated from myo-inositol-OH. It also blurs with APT-amide at 0.5 T (56.9 Hz) and with MT.
  • The amide at 3.5 ppm has no collision warnings and is clean, but it co-resonates with the dominant 250 mM APT amide pool, so it cannot be attributed to GAG specifically.

Direct water saturation: Fast-exchange hydroxyl: swept B1 rises 0.1 to 1.0 µT and direct-sat bandwidth 4.3 to 42.6 Hz. The hydroxyl offset (0.82 ppm = 4.1 Hz at 0.5 T, 57 Hz at 7 T) is INSIDE the direct-saturation bandwidth at 3/5/7 T (31.9/42.6/42.6 Hz), and barely outside at 0.5 T (4.1 vs 4.3 Hz). So the hydroxyl contrast is largely masked by direct water saturation, consistent with the 'fast exchange / poor visibility' regime flags.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat:

  • The amide kex=65.5 s−1 is borrowed from human brain (same class value as APT) - no breast/GAG-specific measurement. The hydroxyl kex=600 s−1 is borrowed from MYO-INOSITOL (PMID 20951217, human brain, 7 T), and that abstract does not even confirm whether the 600 s−1 was phantom or in vivo.
  • The hydroxyl shift (0.825 ppm) is a median of GAG phantom (PMID 30230599) and knee-cartilage (PMID 21460030) values. So the entire GAG hydroxyl simulation rests on a myo-inositol-derived rate - frequently NOT the breast-ECM in-vivo rate. This substantially lowers confidence.

Optimized saturation sequence by field strength (derived from a Bloch-McConnell B1×Tsat sweep):

  • 0.5 T: B1=0.1 µT, Tsat=1500 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.041% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 1.5 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=500 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.089% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 3 T: B1=0.75 µT, Tsat=500 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.207% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 5 T: B1=1 µT, Tsat=750 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.401% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 7 T: B1=1 µT, Tsat=1000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Only 7.0 T hydroxyl reaches the 0.5% threshold (0.581%), and even that is borderline, buried under direct-sat and myo-inositol overlap. Fast exchange favors higher B1 to peak, but at 1.0 µT the 0.82 ppm offset (57 Hz) is inside the 42.6 Hz direct-sat bandwidth, so expect poor specificity. I do not recommend a GAG sequence on these numbers; this entry is given only because the threshold is marginally met. The amide group is below 0.5% at all fields and co-resonates with APT - not separately actionable.
    recommended sequence: 0.581% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied

B1/Tsat vs. extraction method (click for note + literature)

Note:

  • The amide (slow) could use MTRasym but is confounded by the 250 mM APT pool - only multi-pool/AREX fitting would disentangle them. The hydroxyl (fast, offset inside direct-sat, overlapping myo-inositol) is NOT reliably extractable by MTRasym; AREX or multi-pool Lorentzian fitting would be required, and even then GAG-OH vs myo-inositol-OH separation is not achievable at a 0.1 ppm gap.
  • PMID 31728316 notes 7 T is preferred over 3 T for GAG CEST because the hydroxyl is close to water. The glycoNOE rNOE pool is the cleanest GAG handle but was not simulated.

Caveats / critique (8 points, 399 words) — 5 mM as a bulk ECM GAG load is plausible in order of magnitude but is a tissue-averaged figure; in actual breast parenchyma the local ECM GAG is far more dilute…
  • 5 mM as a bulk ECM GAG load is plausible in order of magnitude but is a tissue-averaged figure; in actual breast parenchyma the local ECM GAG is far more dilute than in cartilage. This concentration is the weak point - it sets the (small) simulated amide/hydroxyl contrast. Cartilage gagCEST values do not transfer to breast ECM.
  • Classes are reasonable: N-acetyl amide NH=amide (correct); ring/side OH=hydroxyl (correct); sugar C-H/N-acetyl CH3=rnoe (correct for glycoNOE). BUT the rNOE group was REJECTED by the validator: n_protons=13 flagged as not a per-molecule or per-repeating-unit count, and for a polymer the concentration must be given PER repeating unit, not whole molecule. So the strongest predicted GAG pool (the glycoNOE) is NOT SIMULATED.
  • Agent 2 should re-specify GAG as a per-disaccharide-unit pool. The amide and hydroxyl groups were simulated. No exchangeable group neglected among the simulated ones. The GAG hydroxyl in vivo is ~0.65-1 ppm (PMID 21460030 knee cartilage 0.65 ppm; PMID 30230599 GAG phantom 1 ppm); the simulated 0.825 ppm median is consistent. The N-acetyl amide at 3.5 ppm co-resonates with APT.
  • No breast-specific GAG shift documented. None among simulated groups, but the glycoNOE (sugar C-H) pool - the theoretically cleanest GAG handle - was not simulated due to the per-unit-count rejection and must be re-specified before any claim.

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (ring/side hydroxyl OH (6x) [hydroxyl]: concentration 1-4.26873e+07 mM, kex fixed at 600 s−1 (single measurement, spread unknown)) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 0.01-0.01%, 1.5 T: 0.02-0.02%, 3 T: 0.04-0.04%, 5 T: 0.08-0.08%, 7 T: 0.13-0.13%. Threshold 0.5%.

Frequency-collision analysis:

  • The hydroxyl (0.72 ppm) is the problem: at EVERY field it blurs with the GAG hydroxyl (0.82 ppm; 2.1 Hz at 0.5 T to 29.8 Hz at 7 T, all << the ~223 Hz combined linewidth), so myo-inositol-OH and GAG-OH cannot be separated. At 0.5 T it also blurs with APT-amide (59.1 Hz) and the APT rNOE (89.9 Hz).
  • At higher fields the amide collisions clear (Hz separation grows) but the GAG-OH overlap persists. So myo-inositol is the principal confounder of the GAG hydroxyl.

Direct water saturation: Swept B1 rises 0.1 to 1.0 µT and direct-sat bandwidth 4.3 to 42.6 Hz. The hydroxyl offset (0.72 ppm = 3.6 Hz at 0.5 T, 50 Hz at 7 T) is INSIDE the direct-saturation bandwidth at 3/5/7 T (31.9/31.9/42.6 Hz) and borderline at 1.5 T (10.6 Hz). So the already-tiny hydroxyl contrast is largely masked by direct water saturation, consistent with the 'fast exchange / poor visibility' regime flags.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat:

  • The hydroxyl kex=600 s−1 comes from PMID 20951217 (human brain, 7 T, MICEST) - a single measurement with NO stated range and no stated pH/temperature, and the abstract does not confirm whether k was phantom or in vivo. It is borrowed into breast with no breast-specific measurement, and no uncertainty enters the corners (kex_spread null).
  • Myo-inositol in breast tissue vs brain will differ in pH/T/crowding, so this rate may not be the in-vivo breast rate. Confidence in the (already sub-threshold) contrast is therefore low.

PMID 20951217 (MICEST) is the primary literature for the myo-inositol hydroxyl CEST at 7 T.

  • 1.18 mM is a reasonable MRS-scale tissue value for a phospholipid-intermediate metabolite and consistent with PEA being a breast-cancer proliferation correlate (PE/Pi in PMID 31136039).   • No in-vivo CEST shift for PEA documented anywhere; the reference table has no amine reference, so the ~3.3 ppm amine estimate is unverified and unmeasured. None. The phosphate carries no exchangeable proton and the amine is the only exchangeable group, correctly identified.

In vivo verification: ROI-differential CEST scan — coronal, centered on the upper pole of the left breast (nipple-areola level, a few cm below the clavicle)

Why this scan:

  • A coronal slab through the upper breast captures, top-to-bottom in one FOV and one B1 field, four tissues with known-different APT amide and ECM-GAG concentrations: fibroglandular tissue (target, protein/stroma-rich), pectoralis muscle, breast adipose, and subcutaneous fat. A single saturation scheme is applied to all.
  • If the +3.5 ppm (APT) and +3.2 ppm (GAG N-acetyl amide) MTRasym values track these known concentration gradients across ROIs, the effect is genuine metabolite exchange contrast; a flat or fat-inverted ordering indicates generic MT/NOE background or B1 artifact. Multi-Lorentzian fitting separates the 3.5 vs 3.2 amide components.
ROIWhere it is drawnRole
breast fibroglandular tissue target tissueGlandular/parenchymal lobules of the upper breast, drawn excluding visible fat lobules and the chest wall.Target tissue; highest protein/peptide amide (APT) and stromal ECM GAG concentration.
pectoralis musclePectoralis major muscle on the posterior chest wall, posterior to the gland, drawn well clear of the breast parenchyma.Comparison tissue; mid APT amide (much protein immobilized in sarcomeres), low ECM GAG.
breast adipose tissueIntraparenchymal fat lobules within the breast, drawn away from glandular lobules and chest wall.Comparison tissue; very low APT amide and low ECM GAG.
subcutaneous fatSuperficial fat immediately deep to the skin, anterior to the gland, drawn as a strip over the upper breast.Comparison tissue; low APT amide and low-to-moderate stromal GAG; also a fat-saturation leakage check.

Scan protocol: 3 T, pulsed dual-frequency rectangular (non-selective) pulse train, B1=2 µT, 64 pulses × 400 ms (interpulse delay 100 ms, duty cycle 80%), total Tsat=32000 ms, TR=32250 ms

SAR reasoning (the experimentalist agent's own; the pipeline applies no SAR model): 2.0 µT mean B1 over a duty-cycled train (80% duty, 100 ms gaps) at 3 T keeps whole-body SAR well below 1.5 W/kg. Breast/chest-wall anatomy is high-fat and has a small voxel mass with air-tissue boundaries near the coil, so local specific absorption is limited; the gaps allow tissue cooling. Body-coil chest positioning concentrates any hotspot in low-mass adipose.

Compromise rationale: APT's slow amide exchange is favored: 2.0 µT with 32 s saturation builds a clean, measurable 3.5 ppm exchange peak, consistent with the 3-7 T clinical APT literature. This under-saturates GAG relative to its own 0.75 µT/500 ms optimum, but the N-acetyl amide at 3.2 ppm still exchanges within the train; GAG's real limit is its very small ~0.2% contrast, not B1. The rNOE/glycoNOE pools build at this B1. One B1/Tsat cannot be simultaneously optimal for both exchange regimes.

Fat suppression: SPAIR prepulse (2x SPAIR) plus water-selective excitation on a 3D GRE readout. Breast imaging is dominated by fat: subcutaneous and interspersed intraparenchymal adipose fill most of the slab, and fat's sharp upfield resonances (-1 to -3 ppm) would swamp the rNOE/glycoNOE offsets and bleed into the MTRasym baseline. SPAIR is preferred over STIR for the large fat volume and over spectral-spatial for slab uniformity (fat within ROIs caused artifacts when not suppressed, PMID 22034086).

Motion mitigation:

  • Breast overlies the lung apex and moves with respiration. Use respiratory navigator gating or a short breath-hold per readout of the coronal slab (placed just above the costal margin) to stabilize the fibroglandular and pectoralis ROIs. No cardiac gating (no cardiac ROI).
  • Practical constraint: breath-holds add time per offset across ~20 offsets, and the long 32 s saturation train per offset lengthens each readout; use respiratory-triggered free-breathing if the patient cannot hold breath. Keep the slab thin enough that chest-wall respiratory excursion stays within the readout FOV.

Slice coverage:

  • Coronal slab, 300×250 mm FOV, centered on the upper pole of the left breast (nipple-areola level, a few cm below the clavicle), 30 mm thickness (single slab, or 2×15 mm for higher SNR).
  • Oriented parallel to the chest wall so that, top to bottom, it includes overlying skin/dermis, breast parenchyma (adipose and fibroglandular lobules), and posterior pectoralis major muscle. Technologist to place the slab so the muscle is clearly posterior to the gland and the lung apex is excluded from the central FOV. All four ROIs are drawn on this one slab.

Structures in FOV: breast fibroglandular tissue, breast adipose tissue, subcutaneous fat, pectoralis muscle, skin/dermis (overlying, below slice resolution)

Differential analysis plan:

  • For each ROI, average the Z-spectrum and correct every offset for B0 (separate WASSR map), B1 (transmit map), and water T1/T2 relaxation. Compute MTRasym(3.5) and MTRasym(3.2) = [S(-x)-S(+x)]/S(0), and a multi-Lorentzian fit (3.5 APT peak + 3.2 GAG peak) to separate the two amide components. Build ROI-difference curves: for each metabolite offset plot MTRasym(gland)-MTRasym(fat) and MTRasym(gland)-MTRasym(muscle).
  • Confirmation: the gland-minus-others difference is positive and ordered to match the known concentration ranking (APT: gland > muscle > fat; GAG: gland > others) and, for GAG, the residual after subtracting the 3.5-anchored Lorentzian still shows a gland-preferential 3.2 ppm signal. A flat or fat-inverted ordering means the effect is generic MT/NOE background or B1 artifact.
  • Cross-check against the 0.7x/1.3x B1 re-simulations and the +/-8 ppm baseline: true exchange contrast survives while B1 inhomogeneity scales MTRasym roughly uniformly.

Not actively targeted: Myo-inositol, phosphoethanolamine, phosphocholine, taurine, glutamate, glycine, betaine were not designed around: the physicist agent reported no detectable simulated contrast at any field strength for these in breast, so their amide/guanidyl/hydroxyl exchange at physiologic concentration and 3 T falls below the noise floor. Adding their offsets would cost readout time without discriminating power, so they are outside this scan's budget and contrast threshold.

Caveats:

  • Partial volume: the gland is interspersed with fat lobules and a 30 mm slab cannot resolve thin septa, so fibroglandular ROIs are unavoidably mixed, blurring the concentration gradient and threatening the GAG leg.
  • B0/B1 inhomogeneity is strong and non-uniform across the chest-wall-lung-breast interfaces; even after WASSR and B1-map correction, residual error can mimic or hide small MTRasym differences, especially the ~0.2% GAG signal. Susceptibility at the lung-chest-wall and chest-wall-air interfaces causes off-resonance and edge dropout, so ROIs are kept away from the lung apex.
  • The 2.0 µT/32 s compromise favors APT and under-saturates GAG, so the GAG differential may be weaker than simulated. SPAIR fat-suppression leakage at the upfield rNOE/glycoNOE offsets can contaminate those readouts. A 32 s saturation train per offset with a ~32 s TR lengthens each readout and the whole acquisition, increasing motion and breath-hold burden.
  • Skin/dermis is a genuinely GAG-high tissue but is below slice resolution and not in the MT table, so it is treated qualitatively only.
